MUSIC addresses the challenge of evaluating the quality of multi-turn conversations, which is crucial for developing capable Large Language Models (LLMs), yet remains a significant challenge, often requiring costly human evaluation.

This work was presented at NeurIPS 2025, and the authors are Yihan Wang, Andrew Bai, Nanyun Peng, and Cho-Jui Hsieh.

The researchers discovered that the loss of context awareness occurs in instruction fine-tuned LLMs when the chat template is applied to input prompts. They identify that the performance decline is associated with a bias toward different roles learned during conversational instruction fine-tuning.

The team first demonstrated the loss of context awareness through evaluations of several popular, open-source LLMs using the Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIH) task, showing that while many pretrained models demonstrate near-perfect performance on NIH, their performance deteriorates consistently after SFT.
